info.text:
In the Federal Reserve's 2025 household survey (released May 2026), 63% of adults said they would cover a surprise $400 expense with cash or its equivalent, unchanged since 2022 and down from 68% in 2021. This step-by-step guide builds an emergency fund from zero: what counts as an emergency, how to size the goal in stages (a $500 or $1,000 starter, then one month, then three to six months of essential expenses), finding the first $25 a week and automating it, where the money can live (FDIC and NCUA insurance up to $250,000; the FDIC national average savings rate was 0.38% in mid-2026), workplace emergency savings accounts (contribution balance capped at $2,600 for 2026, adjusted for inflation), and how to use and refill the fund. Worked examples are our own math, and there are no product picks.

News and education, not financial advice.
